advice: Experiment: add a guarded n=512 multiplication path that processes two consecutive k values per iteration. Load both steps' A and B vectors, then apply the four ZA MOPA selectors for k and k+1 in increasing order. Keep the existing full transpose and general predicated path. Enter the fast path only when n==512 and 512 is divisible by 2*svcntsw(), so each tile is full. Hypothesis: fewer loop branches and overlapped vector loads may reduce reduction-loop overhead. This is distinct from the prior one-step constant-bound path and two-step preloaded pipeline: it specializes the n=512 loop and interleaves loads with ordered updates. Advice only; performance is unverified.
risks: Extra live vectors may increase register pressure or cause spills; the compiler may already schedule loads well. Verify compilation with the fixed clang flags, error <=0.002 at n=512, and correctness on odd sizes, sizes that do not tile the streaming vector length, and n<=0 through the general path. Confirm only selectors 0..3 are used and scratch allocation remains inside gemm. Measure serially against fresh AC controls with the frozen workload and repeated-control rules; do not infer a gain from historical battery scores.
